title: API 570 Training in Midland, TX: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 570 exam prep for Permian piping inspectors: gas plant and terminal piping, CUI, CML programmes, injection points, dead legs and sour gas.
h1: API 570 Training in Midland: Piping Inspector Exam Prep for Gas Plant, Terminal and Sour Service Piping
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors across the Midland Basin

Piping is most of what a Permian gas plant is made of. Between the inlet header and the residue gas meter run amine lines, glycol lines, refrigeration loops, NGL product lines, flare headers and hundreds of small-bore connections, and each of them corrodes or cracks at its own pace. Crude terminals in Midland and Crane add tank manifolds, pump suction and discharge piping and the station piping that ties them to the long-haul lines. This page is for inspectors who look after that pipe and are preparing for the API 570 piping inspector examination.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Midland. The API 570 course is self-paced and online: you work through it at your own pace and an instructor answers your questions as they come up. API, the American Petroleum Institute, sets the eligibility rules, administers the exam at Prometric test centres and issues the certification. The course carries no API approval and confers no credential of its own.

Where API 570 applies in the Permian, and where pipeline rules take over

API 570 was developed for petroleum refining and chemical process piping, and it says it may be used, where practical, for other piping systems. Many gas plant and terminal owners adopt it for the piping inside their fences. Outside the fence the picture changes. Energy Transfer's purchase of WTG Midstream in 2024 brought it more than 6,000 miles of gas gathering lines in the Midland Basin, and in 2025 Enterprise agreed to buy about 200 miles of Midland Basin gathering from an Occidental affiliate. Gathering systems and long-haul lines are designed to ASME B31.8 or B31.4 rather than B31.3, and the regulated ones fall under the federal pipeline safety rules in 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195, which the Railroad Commission enforces for intrastate lines in Texas.

The boundary usually sits at a valve or flange where a pipeline enters or leaves a plant or terminal, and the owner's records should say exactly where. An API 570 inspector needs to know where the code stops, so that piping classes, intervals and repair methods are not applied to pipe governed by something else. The guide to the API 570 and pipeline code boundary goes into the detail.

Production leases follow a third set of rules. Under the EPA spill rule at 40 CFR 112.9, an onshore oil production facility with an SPCC plan keeps a written maintenance programme for its flowlines and intra-facility gathering lines, suited to the fluids, corrosivity, volume and pressure, with periodic inspection and testing for leaks and corrosion. That is an owner's programme under a federal rule, not an API 570 requirement, though an API 570 inspector may well be asked to help design it.

Sour gas, amine and the Texas hydrogen sulfide rule

Many Permian gathering systems and plants handle gas that contains hydrogen sulfide, and that shapes piping inspection in three ways.

  • Piping class. API 570 classes piping by the consequence of a leak, and one of its Class 1 examples is a gaseous stream carrying more than 3 percent hydrogen sulfide by weight. Acid gas from the amine regenerator often clears that bar; whether a sour inlet header does depends on the field gas, though the owner can still class it Class 1 on other consequence grounds. Class 1 carries the shortest recommended maximum thickness interval of any piping class, five years.
  • Cracking and corrosion. The API 570 Body of Knowledge tests amine stress corrosion cracking and acidic sour water corrosion from RP 571, alongside chloride and caustic stress corrosion cracking. Lean amine lines, reboiler return piping, regenerator overhead condensate lines and the welds on all of them are where a gas plant piping inspector looks first.
  • Materials. Statewide Rule 36, the Railroad Commission's hydrogen sulfide rule, covers oil, gas and brine operations from production and gathering through processing and storage once the gas carries 100 ppm or more of H2S, and it leaves refineries and petrochemical plants out. On systems whose 100 ppm radius of exposure is more than 50 feet, new construction and modifications must use metal components resistant to sulfide stress cracking under NACE MR-01-75 and API RP 14E, so replacement spools and fittings on a sour plant need material and hardness records to match.

Injection points in a gas plant

A refinery inspector thinks of injection points as wash water, caustic and neutraliser. In a Permian gas plant the list looks different: corrosion inhibitor on inlet and gathering headers, methanol to stop hydrates forming, antifoam dosed into the amine system and chemical treatment on produced-water lines. API 570 defines an injection point as a location where relatively small quantities of material are injected into a process stream, and it treats each one as its own circuit with upstream and downstream limits. A mixing tee, where two process streams join, is not an injection point under that definition.

For the exam, learn the circuit limits, the inspection approach and the recommended maximum thickness interval for injection points from the API 570 edition on your effectivity sheet. For the job, remember that the damage is local. An injected chemical that does not mix well can leave a short, deep corrosion pattern that a widely spaced CML grid will miss, so injection point circuits usually get a denser grid and often a scanning technique rather than spot readings. The injection point inspection guide covers the code rules more fully.

Dead legs in plants that keep growing

Midland Basin processing has grown plant after plant, with second units such as Targa's Greenwood II and Pembrook II following the first, and every expansion of a site leaves pipe behind. Startup and bypass lines, connections for equipment never installed, spare pump lines that sit isolated for months and level bridles all become places where flow stops. API 570 defines a dead leg as a component of a piping system that normally has no significant flow. Water and solids settle there, inhibitor never reaches it, and in produced water or wet gas service bacteria thrive, which is why microbiologically influenced corrosion is one of the RP 571 sections on the API 570 exam.

A dead leg programme starts with finding them, which takes a walk-down with current drawings rather than an isometric review alone. The inspector then decides whether each one stays and is inspected on its own interval, or is removed back to the header. Removal is often the cheaper long-term answer. API RP 574, tested in full on the 570 exam, describes where the corrosion tends to sit, and the dead leg inspection guide sets out a practical approach.

Corrosion under insulation, and soil, in a dry climate

West Texas is semi-arid, and inspectors new to the basin sometimes assume that means little corrosion under insulation. The mechanism needs water at the metal surface and a susceptible temperature, and a gas plant can supply both without much rain. Refrigerated propane loops and cold NGL lines sweat when warm, humid air reaches them through damaged vapour barriers; heat-traced lines cycle in and out of the wet range; and wash-down and fire-water testing soak insulation from outside. CUI is a tested RP 571 section, and the CUI planning guide shows how an inspection plan targets the right locations.

Soil is the other external threat. Where plant piping dips below grade at road crossings or runs buried between units, the soil-to-air interface and the buried length need their own inspection approach. Soil corrosion is also on the exam list, and API 570 sets out how buried piping and soil-to-air interfaces are inspected; the buried piping guide summarises the requirements.

Worked example: a CML on a sour inlet header

Here is an exam-style calculation on a line a Midland inspector might own. The pipe is NPS 8 seamless A106 Grade B, 8.625 in. outside diameter, in sour gas service the owner has classed as Class 1. Design pressure is 1,000 psig at a temperature where the B31.3 allowable stress is 20,000 psi; E and W are 1.0 and Y is 0.4.

  1. Pressure design thickness. B31.3 gives t = PD / [2(SEW + PY)] = (1,000 × 8.625) / [2 × (20,000 + 400)] = 8,625 / 40,800 = 0.211 in. Assume the owner's minimum structural thickness for this size is lower, so 0.211 in. governs.
  2. Rates. One CML read 0.318 in. in 2018, 0.296 in. in 2022 and 0.268 in. in 2026. Long-term rate: (0.318 − 0.268) / 8 = 0.00625 in. a year. Short-term rate: (0.296 − 0.268) / 4 = 0.0070 in. a year.
  3. Remaining life. With the faster short-term rate, (0.268 − 0.211) / 0.0070 = 8.1 years.
  4. Next thickness inspection. API 570 sets the interval at the lesser of half the remaining life and the maximum for the piping class. Half the remaining life is about 4.1 years and the Class 1 maximum is five years, so this CML is due again in about four years.

Two questions follow that the exam will not ask but the owner will. Why has the rate picked up over the last four years, and is this CML representative of the circuit, or is there a worse spot nearby that nobody has measured? On sour inlet piping the answer often lies at low points and just downstream of the inhibitor quill.

Routes into API 570 from Permian jobs

API qualifies candidates on education plus experience gained in the last ten years while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency, ranging from one year of inspection with an engineering or technology degree to five or more years with no formal education. The API 570 certification requirements page lists each route. In Midland, candidates tend to arrive from four directions:

  • UT thickness work. Technicians who have taken CML readings on plant piping for an owner-user inspection organisation or a contractor have the inspection hours the shorter routes ask for, and the certification moves them from recording readings to evaluating them.
  • Pipeline construction and integrity. Welders, welding inspectors and integrity technicians from the gathering and transmission side know pipe well, but their hours may be on B31.4 or B31.8 systems. Describe the work exactly on the application and let API decide what counts. API runs a separate programme, API 1169, for pipeline construction inspectors.
  • Plant operations. Operators and maintenance technicians moving into mechanical integrity bring operating experience and usually need a year of hands-on inspection before they apply.
  • Engineers. Facilities and integrity engineers at midstream companies qualify on the one-year route once they have performed or supervised inspection.

Studying API 570 between field sites

The open-book half of API 570 is a search exercise in B31.3, B16.5 and the other code PDFs on the test centre computer, and repetition, not reading, is what makes you fast at it. A self-paced course lets you practise in short sessions: B16.5 pressure-temperature look-ups on a break between sites, an evening on B31.3 test pressure and weld joint quality factor questions, a day off spent on RP 574 and RP 571. When a look-up will not come out, the instructor answers with the clause that settles it, so the next one is quicker. The course's practice papers copy the closed-book and open-book split of the real exam, which is the best rehearsal for the long day at the test centre.

Sponsoring a piping inspection group from a Midland plant or terminal

A gas plant or terminal with its own API 570 inspectors can keep its piping programme moving between contractor visits: setting circuits, reviewing CML data, deciding intervals and approving repair methods. Employers can enrol several candidates together and point them at the same exam window, and fees are quoted on request. Pair the course with the plant's own data, because candidates who work their practice calculations on real circuits learn the code and the site at the same time.

faq.q: Is there an API 570 class in Midland?
faq.a: There is no Atlantis classroom in Midland. The API 570 course is self-paced online with instructor Q&A, so you study around shifts and site visits and send questions whenever they arise. When API has accepted your application you book a seat at a Prometric test centre; Prometric's locator shows the ones closest to Midland. API issues the certification if you pass.

faq.q: Does gathering pipeline experience count toward API 570?
faq.a: API decides from your application. API 570 is written for process piping, and gathering and transmission lines are designed and regulated under other codes and rules, so hours spent only on pipelines may not be weighed the same way as plant piping inspection. Describe the systems, the codes they were built to and what you did. Many candidates add plant piping experience before they apply.

faq.q: Does Texas require gas plant piping to be inspected by an API 570 inspector?
faq.a: OSHA's process safety management standard, which covers gas plants, does not name a credential. It requires inspection and testing that follow recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices, and many owners adopt API 570 as that practice for their piping. Who may perform and approve the inspections is then set by the owner's programme. The Railroad Commission's Rule 36 sets material requirements for sour service, not inspector qualifications.

faq.q: Is MIC on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Yes. Microbiologically influenced corrosion is one of the RP 571 sections the current API 570 Body of Knowledge tests, along with soil corrosion, CUI, amine cracking, mechanical and vibration-induced fatigue and several others. That list changes between windows, so check the Body of Knowledge for the window you are aiming at before you set your study plan.

faq.q: Which B31.3 edition should I study for API 570?
faq.a: The one listed on the Publications Effectivity Sheet for your exam window. API names the edition of every code and recommended practice it examines, and the Body of Knowledge lists the parts of B31.3 that are excluded. Study from that edition rather than whichever copy your employer keeps, because clause numbers and values can move between editions.

faq.q: Does the course cover small-bore and compressor piping?
faq.a: Yes, as the exam does. Mechanical fatigue, including vibration-induced fatigue, is a tested RP 571 section, and RP 574 covers small-bore and auxiliary piping, both relevant to the reciprocating compressors found across the basin. The course works through those sections with practice questions, and the small-bore piping guide adds the code background.

faq.q: Can I prepare for API 570 while working rotations?
faq.a: That is what a self-paced format is for. There are no fixed class times, so you study on days off and short breaks and pick the material back up where you left it. Plan towards an exam window whose application deadline leaves you enough study time, and use the instructor Q&A for the questions that would otherwise stall you between rotations.

faq.q: Should a Midland piping inspector take API 570 or API 510 first?
faq.a: Take the one that matches the equipment you are responsible for. Piping-heavy roles at gas plants and terminals point to API 570; separator, tower and exchanger work points to API 510. The two share RP 571, RP 577, Section V and Section IX, so the second certification takes less new study than the first.
